<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Our senior secured
credit facility includes a $100.0 million revolving loan facility. As of December&nbsp;30,
2005, we had $3.0 million outstanding on this revolving facility.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Trade accounts payable
of $69.2 million are excluded from the table but generally payable within 30 to
60 days. Accrued interest payable which is currently reocrded as a liability is
also excluded from the table. See Item 8 and the accompanying audited financial
statements </p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;30,
2005, except for operating leases or letters of credit, we have no material
off-balance sheet arrangements.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Seasonality_021809"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Seasonality</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We experience some seasonal
fluctuations as sales of our products typically increase in the second and
third fiscal quarters of the year due to increased apartment turnover and
related maintenance and repairs in the multi-family residential housing
sector during these periods. Typically, November, December&nbsp;and January&nbsp;sales
are lower across most of our brands because customers may defer purchases at
year-end as their budget limits are met and because of the winter holiday
season between Thanksgiving Day and New Year&#146;s Day. Our Copperfield brand,
which we acquired in July&nbsp;2005, experiences approximately 70% of sales
between July&nbsp;and December.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item7a_QuantitativeAndQualitative_021815"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM
7A.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Quantitative
and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are aware of the
potentially unfavorable effects inflationary pressures may create through
higher asset replacement costs and related depreciation, higher interest rates
and higher product and material costs. In addition, our operating performance
is affected by price fluctuations in stainless steel, copper, aluminum, plastic
and other commodities and raw materials. We seek to minimize the effects of
inflation and changing prices through economies of purchasing and inventory
management resulting in cost reductions and productivity improvements as well
as price increases to maintain reasonable profit margins.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that inflation
(which has been moderate over the past few years) did not significantly affect
our operating results or markets in 2005 or 2004. Our results of operations in
2005 and 2004 were </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:18.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">34</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='34',FILE='C:\fc\7314442864_D11236_915339\2204-1-cq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 01:45 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">favorably
impacted by increases in the pricing of certain commodity-based products. Such
commodity price fluctuations have from time to time created cyclicality in our
financial performance, and could continue to do so in the future. In addition,
our use of priced catalogs may not allow us to offset such cost increases
quickly, resulting in a decrease in gross margins and profit.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of our
purchases from foreign-based suppliers are from China and other countries in
Asia and are transacted in U.S. dollars.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivative Financial Instruments</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historically, we entered
into derivative financial instruments from time to time, including interest
rate exchange agreements, to manage our exposure to fluctuations in interest
rates on our debt. In December&nbsp;2004, in conjunction with our Parent&#146;s IPO
we terminated all interest rate exchange agreements, or swaps. Accordingly, at December&nbsp;30,
2005, we did not have any interest rate swap exchange agreements, or swaps. Under
our former swap agreements, we paid a fixed rate on the notional amount to a
bank and the bank paid to us a variable rate on the notional amount equal to a
base LIBOR rate. Our derivative activities, all of which are for purposes other
than trading, are initiated within the guidelines of corporate risk-management policies.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We periodically evaluate
the costs and benefits of any changes in our interest rate risk. Based on such
evaluation, we may enter into new interest rate swaps to manage our interest
rate exposure.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recent Accounting Standards</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2006, the
Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No.&nbsp;155, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Certain Hybrid Financial Instrument&#151;an amendment of FASB
Statements No.&nbsp;133 and 140</font></i>, which resolves issues addressed in
SFAS No.&nbsp;133, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Derivative
Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></i>, Implementation Issue No.&nbsp;D1,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Application of Statement 133 to Beneficial
Interests in Securitized Financial Assets</font></i>. SFAS No.&nbsp;155, among
other things, permits the fair value remeasurement of any hybrid financial
instrument that contains an embedded derivative that otherwise would require
bifurcation; clarifies which interest-only strips and principal-only strips are
not subject to the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;133; and establishes a
requirement to evaluate interests in securitized financial assets to identify
interests that are freestanding derivatives or that are hybrid financial
instruments that contain an embedded derivative requiring bifurcation. SFAS No.&nbsp;155
is effective for all financial instruments acquired or issued in a fiscal year beginning
after September&nbsp;15, 2006. We are currently assessing the impact of SFAS No.&nbsp;155
on our results of operations and financial position.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004,
the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;123R (revised 2004), <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Share-Based
Payment</font></i>, which is a revision of SFAS No.&nbsp;123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R requires all
share-based payments to employees, including grants of employee stock options,
to be recognized in the income statement based on their fair values. This new
standard was to be effective for public companies in the first interim or
annual reporting period beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2005. In April&nbsp;2005,
the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;)&nbsp;adopted a new rule, which
changed the compliance date of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R to the first interim or
annual reporting period of the first fiscal year beginning after June&nbsp;15,
2005. Since our 2005 fiscal year end is December&nbsp;30, this new rule&nbsp;will
not change our scheduled adoption date of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the first day
of our 2006 fiscal year. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R permits public companies to adopt
its requirements using one of two methods:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>A
&#147;modified prospective&#148; method in which compensation cost is recognized
beginning with the effective date (a)&nbsp;based on the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R
for all share-based payments granted after the effective date and (b)&nbsp;based
on the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123 for all awards granted to employees
prior to the effective date of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R that remain unvested on the
effective date.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:18.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">35</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='35',FILE='C:\fc\7314442864_D11236_915339\2204-1-cq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 01:45 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>A
&#147;modified retrospective&#148; method which includes the requirements of the modified
prospective method described above, but also permits entities to restate based
on the amounts previously recognized under SFAS No.&nbsp;123 for purposes of
pro forma disclosures either (a)&nbsp;all prior periods presented or (b)&nbsp;prior
interim periods of the year of adoption.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We plan to use the &#147;modified
prospective&#148; method upon adopting the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R. We
continue to evaluate technical implementation issues relating to the adoption
of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R, including the selection and use of an appropriate
valuation model.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have not yet determined
the impact the adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R will have on our results of
operations for future issuances of share-based payments. The adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R
is expected to result in compensation expense that will reduce net earnings.
The amount of reduction in net earnings will depend on a number of variables,
including, the number of options granted, the vesting periods of options
granted, our stock price and volatility at the date of grant, and employee
exercise behaviors. As of December&nbsp;30, 2005, 2,272,495 stock options are outstanding
of which 2,237,740 are vested and 34,755 are not vested. Accordingly, we have
determined that the adoption of SFAS No. 123R will not have a material effect
on our results of operations associated with these previously issued options. Had
we adopted SFAS No.&nbsp;123R in prior periods, the impact of that standard
would have approximated the impact of SFAS No.&nbsp;123 as described in the
disclosure of pro forma net income and net income (loss) applicable to common
shareholders in &#147;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#148; in the
accompanying notes to the audited consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2004, the
FASB issued Interpretation (&#147;FIN&#148;) No.&nbsp;46(R)-5, Implicit Variable
Interests under FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;46 (revised December&nbsp;2003),
Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities. FIN No.&nbsp;46 (R)-5 is
effective for the first reporting period beginning after March&nbsp;3, 2005;
however, earlier application is permitted for periods for which financial
statements have not yet been issued. We have evaluated the impact of FIN No.&nbsp;46(R)-5
and determined that the impact is immaterial to the consolidated financial
statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2004, the
FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;151, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Amendment of
ARB No.&nbsp;43, Chapter 4</font></i>. This statement amends the guidance in
Accounting Research Bulletin No.&nbsp;43, Chapter 4, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Inventory Pricing</font></i>, to clarify the accounting for abnormal
amounts of idle facility expense, freight, handling costs, and wasted material
(spoilage). This statement requires that those items be recognized as
current-period charges. In addition, this statement requires that allocation of
fixed production overhead to the costs of conversion be based on the normal
capacity of the production facilities. SFAS No.&nbsp;151 is effective for
inventory costs incurred during fiscal years beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2005.
We have evaluated the impact of SFAS No.&nbsp;151 and determined that the
impact will be immaterial to the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2005, the
FASB issued FIN No.&nbsp;47, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for
Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations</font></i>. This interpretation states
that the term &#147;conditional asset retirement obligation&#148; as used in paragraph
A23 of SFAS No.&nbsp;143, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Asset
Retirement Obligations</font></i>, refers to a legal obligation to perform an
asset retirement in which the timing and (or) method of settlement are
conditional on a future event that may or may not be within the control of the
entity. The obligation to perform the asset retirement obligation is
unconditional even though uncertainty exists about the timing and (or) method
of settlement. The effective date for adopting this interpretation is no later
than the end of fiscal years ending after December&nbsp;15, 2005. Our financial
condition, results of operations and cash flows were not impacted by the
adoption of FIN No.&nbsp;47 in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2005, the FASB
issued Statement No.&nbsp;154, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting Changes and Error Corrections&#151;a replacement of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;20
and FASB Statement No.&nbsp;3</font></i>. SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;154 replaces APB
Opinion No.&nbsp;20, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting Changes</font></i>,
and SFAS No.&nbsp;3, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Reporting Accounting
Changes in Interim Financial Statements</font></i>&#151;<i><font style="font-style:italic;">an amendment
of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;28</font></i>, and changes the requirements for the
accounting for and reporting of a change in accounting principle. SFAS No.&nbsp;154
requires retrospective application to prior periods&#146; financial statements of
changes in accounting principle, unless it is impracticable to do so, in which </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:18.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">36</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='36',FILE='C:\fc\7314442864_D11236_915339\2204-1-cq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 01:45 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">case
other alternatives are required. SFAS No.&nbsp;154 is effective for accounting
changes and corrections of errors made in fiscal years beginning after December&nbsp;15,
2005, or for our fiscal 2006&nbsp;year end. We have evaluated the requirements
of SFAS No.&nbsp;154 and has determined that there is no impact on the
consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item8_FinancialStatementsAndSuppl_021840"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM
8.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our consolidated financial
statements are provided in part IV, Item 15 of this filing.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item9_ChangesInAndDisagreementsWi_021843"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM
9.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and
Financial Disclosure</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures_021845"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM
9A.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Controls and
Procedures</font></i></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management, with the
participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer (our
principal executive officer and principal financial officer), evaluated the
effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and
15d-15(e)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) as of December&nbsp;30, 2005. Based
on this evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer
concluded that, as of December&nbsp;30, 2005, our disclosure controls and
procedures were (1)&nbsp;designed to ensure that material information relating
to us, including our consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to our Chief
Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer by others within those entities,
particularly during the period in which this report was being prepared and (2)&nbsp;effective,
in that they provide reasonable assurance that information required to be
disclosed by us in the reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is
recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified
in the SEC&#146;s rules&nbsp;and forms.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Limitations on the Effectiveness of Controls</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management, including
our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, does not expect that
our disclosure controls and procedures or our internal control over financial
reporting will prevent all error and all fraud. A control system, no matter how
well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance that the
objectives of a control system are met. Further, any control system reflects
limitations on resources, and the benefits of a control system must be
considered relative to its costs. Because of the inherent limitations in all
control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that
all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, have been detected. The
design of a control system is also based upon certain assumptions about the
likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will
succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions.
Over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions or
deterioration in the degree of compliance with policies or procedures. Because
of the inherent limitations in a cost-effective control system, misstatements
due to error or fraud may occur and may not be detected. Our disclosure
controls are designed to provide reasonable assurance of achieving their
objectives.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No change in our internal
control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and
15d(f)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) occurred during the quarter ended December&nbsp;30,
2005 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially
affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item9b_OtherInformation_021856"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 9B. </font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Other Information</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></i></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit
Fees.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Consists
of fees billed for professional services rendered for the audit of our
consolidated financial statements and review of interim condensed consolidated
financial statements including quarterly reports. Such fees also include fees
associated with comfort letters and consents in connection with the Refinancing
Transactions completed in 2003 and the IPO transaction in 2004.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit-Related
Fees.</font></i></font>&nbsp;&nbsp; Consists of fees billed for assurance and
related services that are reasonably related to the performance of the audit or
review of our condensed consolidated financial statements and are not reported
under &#147;Audit Fees&#148;. These services include employee benefit plan audits and
accounting consultations in connection with acquisitions and investments and
Sarbanes-Oxley compliance.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tax
Fees.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Consists
of fees for tax services including tax compliance, planning and advice.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All
Other Fees.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Consist
of fees for Sarbanes-Oxley compliance.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our audit committee pre-approves and is responsible
for the engagement of all services provided by our independent auditors.</font></p>

<div>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_082027"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC&#160; ACCOUNTING FIRM</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of<br>
Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc. a New Jersey Corporation<br>
Jacksonville, Florida</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance
sheets of Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc., a New Jersey Corporation, and its
subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;) (a wholly owned subsidiary of Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc.,
a Delaware Corporation) as of December&nbsp;30, 2005 and December&nbsp;31,
2004, and the related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&#146;
equity (deficit) and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended
December&nbsp;30, 2005. These financial statements are the responsibility of
the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these
financial statements based on our audits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the
standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those
standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable
assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material
misstatement. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to
perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. Our audits
included consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis
for designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but
not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the
Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no
such opinion. An audit also includes examining, on a test basis, evidence
supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing
the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as
well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe
that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, such consolidated financial statements
referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial
position of the Company as of December&nbsp;30, 2005 and December&nbsp;31,
2004, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the
three years in the period ended December&nbsp;30, 2005, in conformity with
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</font></p>

<p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">/s/ DELOITTE&nbsp;&amp; TOUCHE, LLP<br>
Certified Public Accountants</font></p>

Jacksonville, Florida</font></p>

<div>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INTERLINE BRANDS, INC. (A NEW JERSEY CORPORATION) AND
SUBSIDIARIES<br>
<a name="NotesToConsolidatedFinancialState_141701"></a>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS<br>
YEARS ENDED DECEMBER 30, 2005, DECEMBER 31, 2004 AND DECEMBER 26, 2003<br>
(In thousands, except share data)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a1_DescriptionOfTheBusiness_085716"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>DESCRIPTION OF THE
BUSINESS</p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc., a New Jersey corporation,
and its subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;) (a wholly owned subsidiary of Interline
Brands,&nbsp;Inc., a Delaware Corporation) is a direct marketer and specialty
distributor of maintenance, repair and operations (&#147;MRO&#148;) products. The Company
sells plumbing, electrical, hardware, security hardware, heating, ventilation
and air conditioning and other MRO products. Interline&#146;s highly diverse
customer base consists of multi-family housing, educational, lodging and health
care facilities, professional contractors and specialty distributors.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company markets and sells its products primarily
through nine distinct and targeted brands. The Company utilizes a variety of
sales channels, including a direct sales force, telesales representatives, a
direct marketing program, brand-specific websites and a national accounts sales
program. The Company provides same day/next day delivery of its products
through its network of regional distribution centers located throughout the
United States and Canada, a national distribution center in Nashville,
Tennessee, vendor managed inventory locations at large professional contractor
customer locations and its dedicated fleet of trucks.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During December&nbsp;2004, a reincorporation merger
occurred and Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc., a Delaware Corporation, (&#147;Interline
Delaware&#148;) became the parent company of its principal operating subsidiary, the
Company. This transaction is described below under &#147;Note 4. Significant
Transactions&#151;Initial Public Offering Transaction.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a2_SummaryOfSignificantAccounting_085809"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>SUMMARY OF
SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Principles of
Consolidation</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>consolidated
financial statements include the accounts of Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc. and
its subsidiaries. These statements have been prepared in accordance with
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Intercompany
balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fiscal Year</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The</font></i></b>  </font>Company
operates on a 52-53 week fiscal year, which ends on the last Friday in
December. The fiscal year ended December&nbsp;30, 2005 was a fifty-two week
year. The fiscal years ended December&nbsp;31, 2004 and December&nbsp;26, 2003
were fifty-three week and fifty-two week years, respectively. References herein
to 2005, 2004, and 2003 are for the fiscal years ended December&nbsp;30, 2005, December&nbsp;31,
2004 and December&nbsp;26, 2003, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and Cash
Equivalents</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Cash</font></i></b>  </font>and
cash equivalents consist of cash and highly liquid investments with an original
maturity of three months or less.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inventories</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Inventories, </font></i></b></font>consisting
substantially of finished goods, are valued at the lower of cost or market. Inventory
cost is determined using the weighted-average cost method. The Company adjusts
inventory for excess and obsolete inventory and for the difference by which the
cost of the inventory exceeds the estimated market value. In order to determine
the adjustments, management reviews inventory quantities on hand, slow movement
reports and sales history reports. Management estimates the required adjustment
based on estimated demand for products and market conditions. To the extent
historical results are not indicative of future results and if events occur
that affect the Company&#146;s relationships with </p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">7</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-7',FILE='C:\fc\6921514413_F25897_904043\2204-1-do.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 10 21:51 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">suppliers or the
salability of their products, additional write-offs may be needed that will increase
cost of sales and decrease inventory.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property and Equipment</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Property </font></i></b></font>and
equipment purchased in the normal course of business is stated at cost, net of
accumulated depreciation and amortization. Expenditures for additions, renewals
and betterments are capitalized. Expenditures for maintenance and repairs are
charged to expense as incurred. Property and equipment acquired in connection
with acquisitions are recorded at fair market value as of the date of the
acquisition. Upon the retirement or disposal of assets, the cost and
accumulated depreciation or amortization is eliminated from the accounts and
the resulting gain or loss is credited or charged to operations. Leasehold
improvements and assets under capital leases are amortized, using the straight-line
method, over the lesser of the estimated useful lives or the term of the lease.
Depreciation and amortization, including assets under capital leases, is
computed using the straight-line method based upon estimated useful lives of
the assets as follows:</p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Costs of Computer
Software Developed or Obtained for Internal Use</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The</font></i></b>  </font>Company
capitalizes costs related to internally developed software in accordance with
Statement of Position (&#147;SOP&#148;) No.&nbsp;98-1, Accounting for the Costs of
Computer Software Developed or Obtained for Internal Use. Only costs incurred
during the development stage, including design, coding, installation and
testing are capitalized. These capitalized costs primarily represent internal
labor costs for employees directly associated with the software development. Upgrades
or modifications that result in additional functionality are capitalized. Approximately
$1.0 million, $0.8 million, and $0.8 million, was capitalized in 2005, 2004,
and 2003, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Goodwill </font></i></b></font>represents
the excess of the costs of acquired companies over the fair value of their net
tangible assets. In accordance with
Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;142, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font></i>, the Company does not amortize goodwill but is required to annually
evaluate goodwill for impairment. Goodwill is tested for impairment at least
annually, or whenever events of changes in circumstances indicate that the
carrying amount may not be recoverable. The Company has elected to perform its
annual goodwill impairment test as of the last day of each year. No impairment
was identified as a result of its impairment test for any year presented.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other Intangible
Assets</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Other </font></i></b></font>intangible
assets include amounts assigned to customer lists, trademarks, deferred debt
issuance costs and non-compete agreements. Other intangibles are amortized on a
straight-line basis over their useful lives, 13 to 40 years for trademarks and
customer lists, and 5 to 10 years for non-compete agreements. Deferred debt
issuance costs are amortized as a component of interest expense over the term of
the related debt using a method that approximates the interest method.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impairment of
Long-Lived Assets</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>Company
evaluates its intangible assets for impairment on an annual basis or when an
event occurs or circumstances change that would indicate that the fair value of
the intangible asset has reduced below its carrying amount. Such evaluations
include an assessment of customer retention, cash flow projections and other
factors the Company believes are relevant. The discounted future expected net
cash flows of each identifiable asset are used to measure impairment losses. The
Company has not identified any impairment losses with respect to long-lived
assets for any year presented.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreign Currency Translation</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Assets </font></i></b></font>and
liabilities of the Company&#146;s foreign subsidiary, where the functional currency
is the local currency, are translated into United States dollars at the year
end exchange </p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">rate. The related
translation adjustments are recorded as a component of other comprehensive
income. Revenues and expenses are translated using average exchange rates
prevailing during the year.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk Insurance</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>Company
has a $0.3 million self-insured retention per occurrence in connection with its
workers&#146; compensation policy (&#147;Risk Insurance&#148;). The Company accrues its estimated
cost in connection with its portion of its Risk Insurance losses using an actuarial
methodology based on claims filed, historical development factors and an
estimate of claims incurred but not yet recorded. The Company discounted its
workers compensation reserve at the rate of 6% at December&nbsp;30, 2005. Claims
paid are charged against the reserve.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimates</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>preparation
of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally
accepted in the United States of America requires management to make estimates
and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and
disclosures of contingent liabilities at the date of the financial statements
and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual
results may differ from those estimates and assumptions.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Concentrations of Credit Risk</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Financial </font></i></b></font>instruments,
which potentially subject the Company to concentration of credit risk, consist
principally of accounts receivable. The Company&#146;s accounts receivable are
principally from facilities maintenance, professional contractor and specialty
distributor customers in the United States and Canada. Concentration of credit
risk with respect to accounts receivable, however, is limited due to the large
number of customers comprising the Company&#146;s customer base. The Company
performs credit evaluations of its customers; however, the Company&#146;s policy is
not to require collateral. As of December&nbsp;30, 2005 and December&nbsp;31,
2004, the Company had no significant concentrations of credit risk.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>carrying
value of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, accounts receivable, and
accounts payable approximate fair value because of the short maturities of
these items. The carrying values of notes payable and long-term debt are
reasonable estimates of their fair values. Estimated fair values of notes
payable and long-term debt are determined by discounting the future cash flows
using rates currently available to the Company for similar instruments. Interest
rate swaps are carried at fair value, which is determined by quoted market
prices.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>Company
recognizes revenue in accordance with Securities and Exchange Commissions (&#147;SEC&#148;)
Staff Accounting Bulletin (&#147;SAB&#148;) No.&nbsp;101, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Revenue
Recognition in Financial Statements, </font></i>as amended by SAB No.&nbsp;104,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition, corrected copy</font></i>. The
SEC requires that the following four basic criteria must be met before the
Company recognizes revenue:</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>persuasive
evidence of an arrangement exists;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>delivery
has occurred or services have been rendered;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the
seller&#146;s price to the buyer is fixed or determinable; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>collectibility
is reasonably assured.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recognizes a
sale when the product has been shipped and risk of loss has passed to the
customer. For goods shipped by third party carriers, the Company recognizes
revenue upon shipment since the terms are generally FOB shipping point. Sales
are recorded net of estimated discounts, rebates and returns. A portion of the
Company&#146;s sales are delivered direct from the suppliers. These direct-shipment
sales are recorded on a gross basis, with the corresponding cost of goods sold,
in accordance with the guidance in Emerging Issues Task Force (&#147;EITF&#148;) No.&nbsp;99-19,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Reporting Revenues Gross as a Principal verses Net
as an Agent</font></i>. The Company provides limited product return and
protection rights to certain customers. The Company accrues product return
reserves and warranty obligations. A provision is made for estimated product
returns based on sales volumes and our experience. Actual returns have not
varied materially from amounts provided historically.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cost of Sales</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Cost </font></i></b></font>of
sales includes merchandise costs, freight-in, and operating costs related to
the Company&#146;s National Distribution Center.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Shipping and
Handling Costs</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Shipping </font></i></b></font>and
handling costs have been included in selling, general and administrative
expenses on the consolidated statements of operations. Such amounts were
approximately $40.6 million, $39.0 million, and $32.5 million in 2005, 2004 and
2003, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising Costs</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Costs </font></i></b></font>of
producing and distributing sales catalogs and promotional flyers are
capitalized and charged to expense over the life of the related catalog and
promotional flyers. Advertising expenses, net of co-op advertising, were
approximately $2.7 million, $2.1 million, and $1.3 million in 2005, 2004 and
2003, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock-Based
Compensation</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;The </font></i></b></font>Company
and its Parent account for stock-based compensation using the intrinsic value
method. Accordingly, compensation cost for stock options issued to employees is
measured as the excess, if any, of the quoted market price of the Parent&#146;s
stock at the date of the grant over the amount an employee must pay to acquire
the stock. Compensation cost for restricted stock issued by Parent to employees
and directors is measured at the fair value on the grant date and is recognized
over the vesting or performance period.</p>

weighted average assumptions used for options granted in 2005 under the 2004
Equity Incentive Plan: dividend yield of 0%, volatility of 29%, risk-free
interest rate of 3.97% and expected life of 5 years. The following weighted
average assumptions were used for options granted in 2004 and 2003 under the
2000 Stock Award Plan. For 2004, dividend yield of 0%, expected volatility of
31%, risk-free interest rate of 3.71%, and expected life of 5 years. For 2003,
dividend yield of 0%, expected volatility of 0%, risk-free interest rate of
4.02%, and expected life of 5 years. The fair value of the 2003 awards
approximated zero.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s revenues and assets outside the United
States are not significant.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income Taxes</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Taxes </font></i></b></font>on
income are provided using an asset and liability approach to financial
accounting and reporting for income taxes. Deferred income tax assets and
liabilities are computed for differences between the financial statement
carrying values and the tax bases of assets and liabilities that will result in
taxable or deductible amounts in the future. Such deferred income tax asset and
liability computations are based on enacted tax laws and rates applicable to
periods in which the differences are expected to affect taxable income. Valuation
allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the
amounts expected to be realized.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivative Financial
Instruments</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Historically, </font></i></b></font>the
Company entered into derivative financial instruments, from time to time,
including interest rate exchange agreements (&#147;Swaps&#148;) to manage its exposure to
fluctuations in interest rates on its debt. Under Swaps the Company held in
2004 and 2003, the Company paid a fixed rate on the notional amount to its
banks and the banks paid the Company a variable rate on the notional amount
equal to a base LIBOR rate. The Company&#146;s derivative activities, all of which
are for purposes other than trading, are initiated within the guidelines of
corporate risk-management policies. See Note 7 for further description of the
Swaps. The Company recorded a gain of $8,232 in 2004 and $5,272 in 2003, as a
result of the change in market value of the Swaps.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reclassifications</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Certain </font></i></b></font>prior
year amounts in the financial statements and the notes have been reclassified
to conform to the 2005 presentation. The reclassifications had no effect on
total stockholders&#146; equity or net income (loss).</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recent Accounting
Standards</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;In </font></i></b></font>February&nbsp;2006,
the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No.&nbsp;155, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Certain Hybrid Financial Instrument&#151;an amendment of FASB
Statements No.&nbsp;133 and 140</font></i>, which resolves issues addressed in
SFAS No.&nbsp;133, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Derivative
Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></i>, Implementation Issue No.&nbsp;D1,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Application of Statement 133 to Beneficial
Interests in Securitized Financial Assets</font></i>. SFAS No.&nbsp;155, among
other things, permits the fair value remeasurement of any hybrid financial
instrument that contains an embedded derivative that otherwise would require
bifurcation; clarifies which interest-only strips and principal-only strips are
not subject to the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;133; and establishes a
requirement to evaluate interests in securitized financial assets to identify
interests that are freestanding derivatives or that are hybrid financial
instruments that contain an embedded derivative requiring bifurcation. SFAS No.&nbsp;155
is effective for all financial instruments acquired or issued in a fiscal year
beginning after September&nbsp;15, 2006. The Company is currently assessing the
impact of SFAS No.&nbsp;155 on its results of operations and financial position.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004,
the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;123R (revised 2004), <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Share-Based
Payment</font></i>, which is a revision of SFAS No.&nbsp;123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R requires all
share-</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">11</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-11',FILE='C:\fc\7314523475_D11236_915339\2204-1-dq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 01:45 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">based
payments to employees, including grants of employee stock options, to be
recognized in the income statement based on their fair values. This new
standard was to be effective for public companies in the first interim or
annual reporting period beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2005. In April&nbsp;2005,
the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;)&nbsp;adopted a new rule, which
changed the compliance date of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R to the first interim or
annual reporting period of the first fiscal year beginning after June&nbsp;15,
2005. Since the Company&#146;s 2005 fiscal year end is December&nbsp;30, this new rule&nbsp;will
not change the Company&#146;s scheduled adoption date of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the
first day of the Company&#146;s 2006 fiscal year. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R permits public
companies to adopt its requirements using one of two methods:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>A &#147;modified
prospective&#148; method in which compensation cost is recognized beginning with the
effective date (a)&nbsp;based on the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R for all
share-based payments granted after the effective date and (b)&nbsp;based on the
requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123 for all awards granted to employees prior to
the effective date of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R that remain unvested on the effective
date.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>A &#147;modified
retrospective&#148; method which includes the requirements of the modified
prospective method described above, but also permits entities to restate based
on the amounts previously recognized under SFAS No.&nbsp;123 for purposes of
pro forma disclosures either (a)&nbsp;all prior periods presented or (b)&nbsp;prior
interim periods of the year of adoption.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company plans to use the &#147;modified prospective&#148;
method upon adopting the requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R. The Company
continues to evaluate technical implementation issues relating to the adoption
of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R, including the selection and use of an appropriate
valuation model.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has not yet determined the impact the
adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R will have on its results of operations for
future issuances of share-based payments. The adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R is
expected to result in compensation expense that will reduce net earnings. The amount
of reduction in net earnings will depend on a number of variables, including,
the number of options granted, the vesting periods of options granted, the
Company&#146;s stock price and volatility at the date of grant, and employee
exercise behaviors. As of December&nbsp;30, 2005, 2,272,495 stock options are outstanding
of which 2,237,740 are vested and 34,755 are not vested. Accordingly, the
Company has determined that the adoption of SFAS No. 123R will not have a
material effect on its results of operations associated with these previously
issued options. Had the Company adopted SFAS No.&nbsp;123R in prior periods,
the impact of that standard would have approximated the impact of SFAS No.&nbsp;123
as described in the disclosure of pro forma net income and net income (loss)
applicable to common shareholders in <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued Interpretation (&#147;FIN&#148;)
No.&nbsp;46(R)-5, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Implicit Variable
Interests under FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;46 (revised December&nbsp;2003),
Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities</font></i>. FIN No.&nbsp;46 (R)-5
is effective for the first reporting period beginning after March&nbsp;3, 2005;
however, earlier application is permitted for periods for which financial
statements have not yet been issued. The Company has evaluated the impact of
FIN No.&nbsp;46(R)-5 and determined that the impact is immaterial to the
consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;151,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Amendment of ARB No.&nbsp;43, Chapter</font></i>.
This statement amends the guidance in Accounting Research Bulletin No.&nbsp;43,
Chapter 4, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Inventory Pricing</font></i>, to
clarify the accounting for abnormal amounts of idle facility expense, freight,
handling costs, and wasted material (spoilage). This statement requires that
those items be recognized as current-period charges. In addition, this
statement requires that allocation of fixed production overhead to the costs of
conversion be based on the normal capacity of the production facilities. SFAS No.&nbsp;151
is effective for inventory costs incurred during fiscal years beginning after June&nbsp;15,
2005. The company has evaluated the impact of SFAS No.&nbsp;151 and determined
that the impact will be immaterial to the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">12</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-12',FILE='C:\fc\7314523475_D11236_915339\2204-1-dq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 01:45 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2005, the FASB issued FIN No.&nbsp;47, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Conditional Asset Retirement
Obligations</font></i>. This interpretation states that the term &#147;conditional
asset retirement obligation&#148; as used in paragraph A23 of SFAS No.&nbsp;143, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Asset Retirement Obligations</font></i>, refers to a
legal obligation to perform an asset retirement in which the timing and (or)
method of settlement are conditional on a future event that may or may not be
within the control of the entity. The obligation to perform the asset
retirement obligation is unconditional even though uncertainty exists about the
timing and (or) method of settlement. The effective date for adopting this
interpretation is no later than the end of fiscal years ending after December&nbsp;15,
2005. The Company&#146;s financial condition, results of operations and cash flows
were not impacted by the adoption of FIN No.&nbsp;47 in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2005, the FASB
issued Statement No.&nbsp;154, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting Changes and Error Corrections&#151;a replacement of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;20
and FASB Statement No.&nbsp;3</font></i>. SFAS No.&nbsp;154 replaces APB Opinion
No.&nbsp;20, Accounting Changes, and FASB Statement No.&nbsp;3, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Reporting Accounting Changes in Interim Financial Statements</font></i>&#151;<i><font style="font-style:italic;">an amendment of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;28,</font></i> and changes the
requirements for the accounting for and reporting of a change in accounting
principle. SFAS No.&nbsp;154 requires retrospective application to prior
periods&#146; financial statements of changes in accounting principle, unless it is
impracticable to do so, in which case other alternatives are required. SFAS No.&nbsp;154
is effective for accounting changes and corrections of errors made in fiscal
years beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2005, or for the Company&#146;s fiscal
2006&nbsp;year end. The Company has evaluated the requirements of SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;154
and has determined that there is no impact on the consolidated financial
statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The acquisition of goodwill during 2005 relates to the
Company&#146;s July&nbsp;2005 acquisition of CCS Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc. This is
discussed in further detail in Note 4. Adjustments to goodwill during 2005 and
2004 relate primarily to the establishment of acquisition accruals for the CCS
and Florida Lighting acquisitions of which $9.5 million relates to the
recording of deferred taxes on the assets and liabilities acquired in the CCS
acquisition. This increase was partially offset by adjustments to acquisition
accruals established for the Barnett and Florida Lighting acquisitions that
were settled for less than the estimated amounts accrued.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
amortization of deferred debt issuance costs, recorded as a component of
interest expense, was $1.6 million, $1.9 million, and $1.8 million in 2005,
2004 and 2003, respectively and write-off of such costs were $2.3 million, $0.7
million and $6.5 million in 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. Amortization
expense on other intangible assets was $4.6 million, $4.0 million and $2.7
million for 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. Expected amortization expense on
other intangible assets (excluding deferred debt issuance costs which will vary
depending upon debt payments) for each of the five succeeding fiscal years is
expected to be as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Change in Estimate</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Effective </font></i></b></font>July&nbsp;1,
2003, the Company changed the estimated useful life of customer lists acquired
in the acquisition of Barnett and Sexauer during September&nbsp;2000 and November&nbsp;1999
respectively, from 40 years to 17 years. The estimated remaining useful life of
17 years was based upon the expected life of the customer accounts acquired
using the attrition rate experienced for the twelve-month period ended September&nbsp;26,
2003, with no consideration given to new accounts generated during this period.
This method is consistent with the guidance provided in SFAS No.&nbsp;142,
which suggests that the customer list intangible asset should be amortized
based on management&#146;s best estimate of its useful life, following the pattern
in which the expected benefits will be consumed or otherwise used up. The
effect of this change in the estimated remaining useful life was not material
to the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">4.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>SIGNIFICANT
TRANSACTIONS</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Initial Public
Offering Transaction</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;In </font></i></b></font>December&nbsp;2004,
Interline Delaware successfully completed its Initial Public Offering and
amended the Company&#146;s senior credit facility. A total of 14,375,000 shares of
the Interline Delaware&#146;s common stock were sold, of which 12,667,000 were sold
by Interline Delaware and 1,708,000 were sold by Interline Delaware&#146;s
shareholders. Interline Delaware sold 12,500,000 shares of </p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">14</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">
