<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">its common stock in December&nbsp;2004
and 167,000 shares in January&nbsp;2005 following the exercise of the
underwriters&#146; over-allotment option. Interline Delaware received $171.8 million
in net proceeds including the exercise of the underwriters&#146; over-allotment
option, representing $176.9 million of proceeds from the sale of stock net of
underwriting discounts and commissions, less $4.1 million of initial public
offering costs and $1.1 million of debt issuance costs. &#160;After the IPO-related expenses and preferred
stock consideration in the reincorporation merger were paid, all of the proceeds
from the IPO were contributed to the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Immediately prior to the closing of the IPO, a
reincorporation merger occurred and the Company became a wholly owned
subsidiary of Interline Delaware. In the reincorporation merger, the holders of
the preferred stock of the Company received an aggregate of $55 million in cash
and 19,183,321 shares of Interline Delaware&#146;s common stock and the holders of
the common stock of the Company received a total of 66,667 shares of Interline
Delaware&#146;s common stock. In addition, holders of options to purchase shares of
the common stock of the Company were converted into options to purchase shares
of Interline Delaware&#146;s common stock. As part of the reincorporation merger,
Interline Delaware received 100 shares of Company common stock and one share of
Company preferred stock, representing all of the authorized and outstanding
shares of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company also used $31.3 million of the
contribution from Parent from proceeds of its IPO to partially repay the term
loan under its credit facility. The Company amended its senior credit facility
to allow for the IPO and reduce the interest rate applicable to the Company&#146;s
term loans. In conjunction with this amendment, the Company incurred $1.1
million of debt issuance costs. In December&nbsp;2004, the Company also used
$4.6 million of the proceeds to terminate the interest rate swap agreements. In
January&nbsp;2005, the Company used $70.0 million of the proceeds from the IPO
transaction to partially redeem its 11.5% senior subordinated notes. In
connection with the redemption, the Company paid $8.1 million of premiums for
early redemption of the senior subordinated notes and recorded a $10.3 million
loss on the early extinguishment of debt, which included a charge for write-off
of unamortized debt issuance costs in the amount of $2.3 million in January&nbsp;of
2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the Parent&#146;s IPO transaction, the
Company paid bonuses totaling $6.2 million and incurred additional compensation
expense for the forgiveness of shareholder loans of $1.9 million and the
reimbursement of taxes of $1.1 million on such loan forgiveness. These costs
are reported as IPO related expenses in the Statements of Operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Special Costs and
Expenses</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;Special </font></i></b></font>costs
and expenses for 2003 and 2002 consist of costs associated with distribution
center consolidation, relocation, lease termination, severance related costs
and other transaction fees. Such costs and expenses were $0.0 million, $0.0
million and $0.6 million for years 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Barnett Acquisition</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;In </font></i></b></font>September&nbsp;2000,
the Company completed the acquisition of Barnett,&nbsp;Inc. (the &#147;Barnett
Acquisition&#148;) for an aggregate purchase price of $220.8 million including costs
of acquisition of approximately $7.1 million. The costs of acquisition include a $3.0 million advisory fee paid to a
significant stockholder of the Company. Goodwill recorded in connection
with the Barnett Acquisition totaled approximately $89.3 million. Other
intangible assets recorded in connection with the Barnett Acquisition totaled
approximately $53.1 million. During
2001, the Company finalized its purchase price of Barnett and as a result
recorded an increase in goodwill of approximately $12.3 million. These additional
costs relate to the closure of duplicate Barnett facilities, severance related
to these closures and the relocation and integration of Barnett employees and
administrative functions. As of December&nbsp;30, 2005 and December&nbsp;31,
2004, $2.2 million and $3.1 million were accrued for such costs, respectively,
in accordance with EITF No.&nbsp;95-3, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Recognition
of Liabilities in Connection with a Purchase Business Combination</font></i>.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Florida Lighting
Acquisition</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;On </font></i></b></font>November&nbsp;24,

Lighting Acquisition&#148;), which sells residential lighting and electrical </p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The aggregate purchase price was $23.1 million

goodwill of approximately $3.3 million. These additional costs primarily relate
to the integration of Florida Lighting systems and operations. As of December&nbsp;30,

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill recorded in connection with the acquisition
of Copperfield is not expected to be deductible for tax purposes.&#160; The intangible assets are subject to
amortization and will be amortized on a straight-line basis over a weighted-average
useful life of approximately 22.3 years.&#160;
The Company recorded an addition to goodwill of $9.5 million in
connection with the acquisition of Copperfield to recognize the book to tax
basis difference on non-goodwill intangibles.&#160;
Supplemental pro forma information has not been provided below because
it is immaterial.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a5_AccountsReceivable_090658"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>ACCOUNTS
RECEIVABLE</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s trade
receivables are exposed to credit risk. The majority of the market served by
the Company is comprised of numerous individual accounts, none of which is
individually significant. The Company monitors the creditworthiness of its
customers on an ongoing basis and provides a reserve for estimated bad debt
losses.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The activity in the
allowance for doubtful accounts consisted of the following:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2003, the Company completed an offering of
$200 million of 11.5% senior subordinated notes due 2011 (the &#147;11.5% Notes&#148;)
and entered into a $205.0 million senior secured credit facility which
consisted of a $140.0 million term loan facility and a $65.0 million revolving
loan facility, a portion of which is available in the form of letters of credit.
The net proceeds from the offering of senior subordinated notes and the
refinancing of the former credit facility with the new credit facility were
used to: (1)&nbsp;repay all outstanding indebtedness under the Company&#146;s former
credit facility, (2)&nbsp;redeem all the 16% senior subordinated notes, (3)&nbsp;pay
accrued interest and related redemption premiums on the Company&#146;s former debt
and (4)&nbsp;pay transaction fees and expenses. These transactions are
hereafter referred to as the Refinancing Transactions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The $200 million principal amount 11.5% senior
subordinated notes due 2011 pay interest each May&nbsp;15 and November&nbsp;15,
with the first payment made on November&nbsp;15, 2003. Prior to May&nbsp;15,
2006, the Company may redeem up to 35% of the notes using proceeds of certain
equity offerings and the Company may redeem all of the notes after May&nbsp;15,
2007, subject to redemption premiums unless redeemed after May&nbsp;15, 2009. &#160;The Company elected to redeem $70.0 million of
the 11.5% senior subordinated notes using proceeds from the IPO transaction and
gave the 30-day notice, required by the indenture agreement, on December&nbsp;20,
2004. In January&nbsp;2005, the Company recorded a loss on extinguishment of
debt of $10.3 million, consisting of the write-off of deferred financing costs
of $2.3 million and the premium of $8.1 million on the $70.0 million redemption
of 11.5% senior subordinated notes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the Company amended its term
loan facility and revolving loan facility. The term loan was reduced to $100.0
million from $140.0 million and the revolving loan facility was increased to
$100.0 million from $65.0 million. As part of the amendment in December&nbsp;2004,
the Company paid down $31.3 million of the term loan using proceeds from
Interline Delaware&#146;s IPO. The Company also amended its credit facility on July&nbsp;7,
2005, to permit the incurrence of an additional $50.0 million term loan, having
substantially the same terms as the existing term loan in connection with the
Copperfield acquisition, discussed below. On August&nbsp;8, 2005, the Company
again amended its credit facility to lower the interest rate spreads applicable
to the additional $50.0 million term loan. The amended credit facility provides
for aggregate commitments of $250.0 million, consisting of (1)&nbsp;a revolving
loan facility of $100.0 million, of which a portion not exceeding $20.0 million
will be available in the form of letters of credit, and (2)&nbsp;a term loan
facility of $150.0 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowings under the amended term loan facility and
revolving loan facility bear interest, at the Company&#146;s option, at either LIBOR
plus a spread or at the alternate base rate plus a spread. The indebtedness
under the amended credit facility is guaranteed by the Company and by our
domestic subsidiaries. Interest rates in effect on borrowings under the term
loan facilities at December&nbsp;30, 2005 ranged from 6.79% for LIBOR based
borrowings and 8.5% for prime based borrowings under the $100.0 million tranche
B-1 term loan and 6.29% for LIBOR based borrowings and 8.25% for prime
based borrowings under the $50.0 million tranche B-2 term loan. Outstanding
letters of credit under the revolving loan facility are subject to a per annum
fee equal to the applicable spread over the adjusted </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">18</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-18',FILE='C:\fc\73211938407_H10036_920703\2204-1-du.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 21:19 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">LIBOR for revolving loans.
The term loan facility matures on December&nbsp;31, 2010 and the revolving loan
facility matures on May&nbsp;31, 2008. Debt issuance costs capitalized in
connection with the amended credit facility were approximately $1.1 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;30, 2005, the Company had $86.4
million available under its revolving loan facility. Total letters of credit
issued under this facility as of December&nbsp;30, 2005 were $10.6 million. There
were $3.0 million of borrowings under the revolving loan facility at December&nbsp;30,
2005. The credit facility is secured by substantially all of the assets of the
Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Debt issuance costs capitalized in connection with the
Refinancing Transactions were approximately $13.1 million. An expense of
approximately $14.9 million for the early extinguishment of debt resulted from
the write-off of the unamortized loan fees and loan discount relating to the
Company&#146;s former credit facility and the redemption premium incurred upon
redemption of the 16% senior subordinated notes, as part of the Refinancing
Transactions. Debt issuance costs capitalized in connection with the amended
credit facility were approximately $1.1 million. An expense of approximately
$0.7 million for early extinguishments of debt resulted from the write-off of
the unamortized loan fees relating to the Company&#146;s former credit facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historically, the Company and/or the Parent entered
into derivative financial instruments from time to time, including interest
rate exchange agreements, to manage its exposure to fluctuations in interest
rates on its debt. All interest rate swap agreements were terminated as of December&nbsp;2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The credit facility contains customary affirmative and
negative covenants that limit the Company&#146;s ability to incur additional
indebtedness, pay dividends on its common stock or redeem, repurchase or retire
its common stock or subordinated indebtedness, make certain investments, sell
assets, and consolidate, merge or transfer assets, and that require the Company
to maintain a maximum debt to cash flow ratio and a minimum interest expense
coverage ratio. The Company was in compliance with all covenants at December&nbsp;30,
2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2003, the Company issued a non-recourse
note payable in the principal amount of $3.3 million for the purchase of an
investment. This note, which is secured only by the investment, bears interest
at a rate of 4% per annum, with principal due in full in April&nbsp;2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
maturities of long-term debt subsequent to December&nbsp;30, 2005 are as
follows:</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8.&nbsp;&nbsp; PREFERRED STOCK</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has the
authority to issue one share of preferred stock, par value $.01 per share. At December&nbsp;30,
2005 and December&nbsp;31, 2004, there was one preferred share issued and
outstanding, held by the Parent. &#160;In
connection with the reincorporation merger and IPO transaction, as described
above, the holders of the preferred stock of the Company received an aggregate
of $55 million in cash and 19,183,321 shares of Interline Delaware&#146;s common
stock and one share of Company preferred stock was issued to the Parent,
representing all authorized and outstanding shares of preferred stock of the
Company. The preferred stock is stated at its liquidation value plus accrued
dividends. As holder of the preferred stock, Interline Delaware is entitled to
receive dividends payable at the annual rate of 14%. All dividends </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">19</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)&nbsp;accrue
on a daily basis, (2)&nbsp;are cumulative, whether or not earned or declared, (3)&nbsp;are
compounded quarterly from the date of issuance of such shares and (4)&nbsp;are
declared payable when declared by the Board of Directors. All dividends accrued
are payable prior to the payment of any dividend on shares of any junior stock.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9.&nbsp;&nbsp; STOCKHOLDERS&#146;
EQUITY</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Common Stock</font></i></b><font style="font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">During 2004, Interline Delaware completed its IPO described in Note 4
above. In addition to the shares issued to the public at the IPO in December&nbsp;2004.
Interline Delaware issued 19,250,000 shares of its common stock to existing
stockholders and senior management of the Company in connection with the
reincorporation merger and the IPO. Existing holders of the Company&#146;s common
stock received .01218 shares of Interline Delaware&#146;s common stock per share held
or an aggregate of 66,667 shares of common stock. Interline Delaware received
100 common shares of the Company, representing all authorized and outstanding
shares of common stock of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stockholder Loans</font></i></b><font style="font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">In conjunction with the IPO transaction described in Note 4 above, the
Company forgave $1.6 million of stockholder loans included in stockholders&#146;
equity and accordingly took a charge to operating income for this amount. As of
December&nbsp;16, 2004, the date the loans were forgiven, and December&nbsp;26,
2003, $375 and $345, respectively, of interest was accrued on the notes and was
included as a portion of the stockholder loans in stockholders&#146; equity. As of December&nbsp;30,
2005 and December&nbsp;31, 2004, there were no stockholder loans outstanding.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a1_105432"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>PROFIT
SHARING PLAN</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has qualified
profit sharing plans under Section&nbsp;401(k)&nbsp;of the Internal Revenue
Code. Contributions to the plans by the Company are made at the discretion of
the Parent&#146;s Board of Directors. Company contributions to the plans were
approximately $1.2 million, $1.1 million and $0.7&nbsp;million for 2005, 2004
and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a11_CommitmentsAndContingencies_105434"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>COMMITMENTS AND

 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">20</font></p>

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-20',FILE='C:\fc\73211938407_H10036_920703\2204-1-du.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 21:19 2006' -->



<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the Copperfield acquisition, the
Company leases an office building from an entity in which an employee and his
family hold an ownership interest in the property. This lease was amended in November&nbsp;2005
and will expire on November&nbsp;30, 2010, with an option to extend for one
additional five year term. Minimum annual rent payable under this lease is
approximately $153, plus all real estate taxes and assessments, and all
operating costs related to the building. The total rent expense for this lease
was approximately $72 in 2005 since the closing of the Copperfield acquisition.
The Company believes that the terms of the lease are no less favorable to it
than could be obtained from an unaffiliated party.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company operates a distribution center, which is
leased from an entity, which was partially owned by a stockholder and former
director of the Company. The former officer sold his ownership interest in the
property in September&nbsp;2002. Minimum annual rent payable under this lease
is approximately $308, plus all real estate taxes and assessments, utilities
and insurance related to the premises. Total rent expense for this lease was
approximately $308 in both 2005 and 2004 and $289 in 2003. This lease expires
on May&nbsp;31, 2006 and does not contain any renewal terms. The Company
believes that the terms of the lease are no less favorable to it than could be
obtained from an unaffiliated party.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company previously leased an office building from
a stockholder and former director of the Company. As amended in March&nbsp;1995,
under the terms of the lease, the Company was required to pay approximately
$137 annually, plus all real estate taxes and assessments, utilities and
insurance related to the premises. Total rental expense for this lease was $85
for 2004 and $137 for 2003. The lease expired July&nbsp;31, 2004 and the
Company did not renew its lease and relocated as of July&nbsp;2004. The Company
believes that the terms of the lease were no less favorable to it than could be
obtained from an unaffiliated party.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rent expense under all operating leases was
approximately $19.1 million, $17.7 million, and $15.7 million for 2005, 2004
and 2003, respectively. Certain of the leases provide that the Company pays
taxes, insurance and other operating expenses applicable to the leased
premises.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employment
Agreement</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">The </font></i></b></font>Company
(including the Parent for the benefit of the Company) has employment agreements
with certain officers of various dates through 2006, unless terminated earlier
by the Company and/or the Parent, at combined salaries of $4.2 million, plus
bonuses and subject to adjustments.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management
Agreement</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">In</font></i></b></font> May&nbsp;2000,
the Company entered into an advisory agreement with a significant stockholder
of the Company, which provides for an annual advisory fee of $250 plus out-of-pocket
expenses of up to $25 per year. The management agreement was terminated in December&nbsp;2004
in conjunction with the Parent&#146;s IPO.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Contingent
Liabilities</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">At</font></i></b>  </font>December&nbsp;30,
2005 and December&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company was contingently liable for unused
letters of credit aggregating approximately $10.6 million and $8.7 million,
respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal Proceedings</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">The</font></i></b>  </font>Company
and its Parent are involved in various legal proceedings in the ordinary course
of its business that are not anticipated to have a material adverse effect on
the Company&#146;s results of operations or financial position.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a12_StockbasedCompensationPlans_075657"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12.&nbsp;&nbsp; STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION PLANS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2000, the Company established a Stock Award
Plan, (the &#147;2000 Plan&#148;), under which the Company was authorized to award a
total of 525,000 shares (6,395 after the reorganization described in Note 4) of
common stock in the form of incentive stock options (which may be awarded to
key employees only), nonqualified stock options, stock appreciation rights, or
SARs, and restricted stock awards, all of which may be awarded to directors,
officers, key employees and consultants. The exercise price per share for an
incentive stock option may not be less than 100% of the fair market value of a
share of common </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">21</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-21',FILE='C:\fc\73202136459_H10036_920703\2204-1-dw.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 14 20:21 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">stock on the grant date. The
exercise price per share for an incentive stock option granted to a person
owning stock possessing more than 10% of the total combined voting power of all
classes of stock may not be less than 110% of the fair market value of a share
of common stock on the grant date, and may not be exercisable after the
expiration of ten years from the date of grant. The Parent&#146;s compensation
committee will determine in its sole discretion whether a SAR is settled in
cash, shares or a combination of cash and shares. As discussed in Note 4, the
stock options issued under the 2000 Plan were converted into stock options of
Interline Delaware.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, the Parent adopted the 2004 Equity
Incentive Plan, (the &#147;2004 Plan&#148;), under which the Parent may award 3,175,000
shares in the form of incentive stock options, nonqualified stock options,
stock appreciation rights, or SARs, restricted share units, restricted stock
and stock bonus awards, all of which may be awarded to any employee, director,
officer or consultant of the Company or the Parent. Under the terms of the 2004
Plan and unless the compensation committee of the Parent determines otherwise,
the exercise price of the options will not be less than the fair market value
of the common stock of Interline Delaware at the time of grant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon completion of the Parent&#146;s IPO in December&nbsp;2004,
175,820 shares of its restricted stock were issued to senior management. The
restricted stock awards will vest contingent upon the executive&#146;s continued
employment in one-third installments over three years provided that certain
pre-established annual percentage increases in our earnings per share are
attained. The restricted stock will also vest if the executive remains in our
employ for seven years on the seventh anniversary of the date of grant. In
addition, an aggregate of 10,000 shares of the Parent&#146;s restricted stock were
issued to two non-employee directors who are not affiliated with any of our
principal stockholders. Such awards will vest over two years. As a result of
these restricted stock awards, the Company will incur non-cash charges between
$0.4 million and $0.9 million in each of the next two to six years depending
upon the acceleration of vesting of restricted stock. These two directors also
received 20,000 non-qualified stock options with an exercise price equal to the
IPO price of $15.00 per share. In addition, the Parent issued to management
1,835,218 non-qualified stock options to purchase the Parent&#146;s common stock
with an exercise price equal to the IPO price of $15.00 per share and 590,465
non-qualified stock options to purchase the Parent&#146;s common stock with a
weighted average exercise price of $24.00 per share. All of these options were
fully vested and exercisable when granted. However, management will only be
permitted to sell shares acquired upon the exercise of the options in 25%
increments over four years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A
summary of the status of stock option plans to purchase the Parent&#146;s common
stock is as follows:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a15_SubsidiaryGuarantors_094042"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15.</font></b><font face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>SUBSIDIARY
GUARANTORS</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company completed an offering of $200 million
principal amount of 11.5% senior subordinated notes in connection with its
Refinancing Transactions in 2003, of which $130 million principal amount
remains outstanding. The Company filed a registration statement with the
Securities and Exchange Commission with respect to an exchange offer for the
11.5% senior subordinated notes and with respect to resales of the senior
subordinated notes by an affiliate of the Company for market-making purposes. The
registration statement was declared effective by the SEC and the exchange offer
was consummated. The Company&#146;s 11.5% senior subordinated notes are fully and
unconditionally guaranteed, jointly and severally, on a subordinated basis by
Wilmar Holdings,&nbsp;Inc., Wilmar Financial,&nbsp;Inc., Glenwood Acquisition
LLC, and CCS Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc. (100%-owned subsidiaries of the Company),
together with Copperfield Chimney Supply,&nbsp;Inc. and Riverton Machine
Foundry,&nbsp;Inc. (100%-owned subsidiaries of CCS Enterprises,&nbsp;Inc.). The
guarantees by these subsidiary guarantors (the &#147;Subsidiary Guarantors&#148;) are
senior to any of their existing and future subordinated obligations, equal in
right of payment with any of their existing and future senior subordinated
indebtedness and subordinated to any of their existing and future senior
indebtedness. Accordingly, condensed consolidating financial statements for
Interline Brands,&nbsp;Inc. and the Subsidiary Guarantors are presented below.</font></p>
